security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI configures PMP/ePMP entries covering a shared interrupt vector table (CLIC/CLINT) that grants S-mode more than execute-only permission (e.g., R=1 or W=1 under L=0 standard PMP, or misconfigured Smepmp L=1 shared-code region), exposing M-mode interrupt handler pointers to lower privilege levels.
security_spec.summary: If OpenSBI grants S-mode read access to a shared CLIC vector table via PMP, S-mode can leak M-mode interrupt handler addresses; if write is granted, S-mode can redirect M-mode interrupt handling to arbitrary code.

findings.finding: Catch-all domain memory region (0x0–~0UL) grants S/U-mode full R/W/X under both standard PMP and Smepmp. On a CLIC platform with Smivt shared vector tables, any mivt/meivt-pointed memory in this region is readable and writable by S-mode, exposing M-mode interrupt handler pointers.

spec_citations.excerpt: If xivt or xeivt is configured such that multiple privilege levels share a single vector table, the memory protection units (e.g., PMP, Smepmp) must grant execution permission to the shared vector table for all applicable lower privilege levels. For standard PMP: a PMP entry with L=1, R=0, W=0 and X=1 permits both privilege levels to execute from the table while preventing modifications. For Smepmp: Setting L=1, R=0, W=1 and X=0 grants both M-mode and S-mode execute only permission to the vector table.

findings.finding: Entire peripheral port (0x0–0x80000000, 2GiB) is registered as SURW_MRW (shared read/write for M and S/U). Under Smepmp MML=1, this produces pmp_flags = PMP_W|PMP_X, granting S-mode read/write access. If a CLIC vector table (mivt/meivt) resides in this 2GiB range, M-mode interrupt handler pointers are exposed to S-mode.

spec_citations.excerpt: If xivt or xeivt is configured such that multiple privilege levels share a single vector table, the memory protection units (e.g., PMP, Smepmp) must grant execution permission to the shared vector table for all applicable lower privilege levels. [...] For Smepmp: Setting L=1, R=0, W=1 and X=0 grants both M-mode and S-mode execute only permission to the vector table.

findings.finding: System port region (512GiB–1TiB, RV64 only) is also registered as SURW_MRW shared R/W. Same exposure as the peripheral port: any CLIC vector table in this range grants S-mode read/write access to M-mode interrupt handler pointers.

SUX_MRX shared execute-only-for-S/U encoding (PMP_L|PMP_W|PMP_X) exists in the domain flag system and is the correct Smepmp encoding for protecting a shared interrupt vector table per ACLIC spec (L=1,R=0,W=1,X=0). However, no OpenSBI code uses SUX_MRX to protect any memory region, least of all CLIC vector tables, because OpenSBI has no CLIC/mivt awareness.

spec_citations.excerpt: Under the Smepmp extension, the shared vector table can be secured as a 'Locked Shared code region'. Setting L=1, R=0, W=1 and X=0 grants both M-mode and S-mode execute only permission to the vector table.

findings.finding: Under standard (non-Smepmp) PMP, SU_READABLE/WRITABLE/EXECUTABLE flags map directly to PMP_R/PMP_W/PMP_X with L=0. This means the catch-all region grants S/U-mode full R/W/X while M-mode retains default full access. For a shared CLIC vector table under standard PMP, the ACLIC spec requires at minimum L=1,R=0,W=0,X=1 (execute-only) to prevent S-mode modification of vector table entries.

spec_citations.excerpt: For a system with M-mode and S-mode, a PMP entry with L=1, R=0, W=0 and X=1 permits both privilege levels to execute from the table while preventing modifications. If L=0, S-mode retains execute only permission while M-mode maintains full permissions.

findings.finding: csr_set(CSR_MSECCFG, MSECCFG_MML) activates ePMP encoding, but there is no prior audit of whether any shared region covers CLIC vector table memory. Once MML is set, all SURW_MRW regions (shared R/W) that overlap vector table memory grant S-mode read/write access to M-mode interrupt handler pointers with no carve-out possible.
findings.snippet:
/* Set the MML to enforce new encoding */
csr_set(CSR_MSECCFG, MSECCFG_MML);

findings.finding: CSR definitions for CLIC vector table registers are absent: no CSR_MIVT (0x307), CSR_MEIVT (0x308), CSR_SIVT (0x107), CSR_SEIVT (0x108), or CSR_MNXTI. Without these CSR definitions, OpenSBI cannot detect, configure, or protect CLIC interrupt vector table memory regions.

spec_citations.excerpt:
Number  Name   Description
0x305   mtvec  M-mode Trap-handler base address / interrupt mode
(NEW) 0x307   mivt   M-mode Interrupt-handler vector table base address
(NEW) 0x308   meivt  M-mode External Interrupt-handler vector table base address
0x105   stvec  S-mode Trap-handler base address / interrupt mode
(NEW) 0x107   sivt   S-mode Interrupt-handler vector table base address
(NEW) 0x108   seivt  S-mode External Interrupt-handler vector table base address

findings.finding: mstateen0 bit definitions exist for IMSIC (bit 58) and AIA (bit 59) but the ACLIC bit (bit 53 per spec) is missing. Without SMSTATEEN0_ACLIC, OpenSBI cannot gate S-mode access to ACLIC indirect CSRs (sivt, seivt, spistatus, sithreshold, sspcs, acliciprio, aclicsourcecfg), and cannot enable ACLIC-specific mstateen0 protections.

spec_citations.excerpt: If the Smstateen extension is implemented, then the bit 53 (ACLIC) in mstateen0 is implemented. If bit 53 (ACLIC) of a controlling mstateen0 CSR is zero, then access to the new CSRs (acliciprio[k], aclicsourcecfg[k]) by S-mode or a lower-privilege mode results in an illegal instruction exception.

findings.finding: Extension detection probes CSR_MTOPI for SBI_HART_EXT_SMAIA only. There is no detection for Smip/Smaclic/Ssaclic extensions. Without a CLIC-aware feature flag, there is no conditional branch to configure vector-table-aware PMP entries or ACLIC mstateen0 bits.

Trap vector setup unconditionally writes the raw _trap_handler address to CSR_MTVEC (mtvec.MODE=0, Direct mode). No CLIC vector mode (mtvec.MODE=3) is configured. If a prior boot stage set mivt/meivt to point to shared memory, those CSRs remain active but unprotected—OpenSBI neither reads, clears, nor protects them with PMP entries.
findings.snippet:
lla	a4, _trap_handler
csrr	a5, CSR_MISA
srli	a5, a5, ('H' - 'A')
andi	a5, a5, 0x1
beq	a5, zero, _skip_trap_handler_hyp
lla	a4, _trap_handler_hyp
_skip_trap_handler_hyp:
csrw	CSR_MTVEC, a4

findings.finding: T-Head C9xx defines THEAD_C9XX_CSR_NT_MTVT (0xbe4), a vendor-specific CLIC-style interrupt vector table base CSR. OpenSBI never reads, writes, or protects this CSR with PMP entries. If a prior boot stage configured NT_MTVT to point to memory subsequently mapped as shared R/W, S-mode can read and modify M-mode interrupt handler pointers.

The dynamic PMP mapping function hardcodes pmp_flags = PMP_W|PMP_X (shared R/W for M and S/U under MML=1). There is no option to create a shared execute-only (SUX_MRX, PMP_L|PMP_W|PMP_X) mapping that would be appropriate for a vector table region. Any use of map_range for vector table memory would inadvertently grant S/U-mode read access.
findings.snippet:
/* shared R/W access for M and S/U mode */
unsigned int pmp_flags = (PMP_W | PMP_X);

findings.finding: Domain registration validates firmware region ordering (fw_region_inited) but performs no overlap check for CLIC/CLINT vector table memory. Any MMIO or shared region can silently overlap the vector table address range, granting S-mode unintended read/write permissions.

SURW_MRW flag combination maps to PMP_W|PMP_X under Smepmp MML=1, meaning shared read/write for both M and S/U. This is the encoding used by SiFive and ESWIN platform port configurations for all peripheral MMIO regions. Any CLIC vector table in a SURW_MRW region is fully readable and writable by S-mode.
